title: Apache Kafka (Topics, Partitions, Consumer Groups)
intro: Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform built as an append-only commit log, supporting millions of events per second with strict per-partition ordering.
objectives: Deconstruct Kafka's fundamental storage unit: the partitioned append-only commit log.
Analyze consumer group rebalancing and distributed partition assignment.
Achieve zero-copy high throughput using Linux sendfile and sequential disk I/O.
body:
### Partitioning & Order Guarantees
A Kafka Topic is divided into multiple **Partitions**. Kafka guarantees strict total ordering **only within a single partition**, not across partitions. Producers specify a Partition Key (e.g. `order_id` or `user_id`); all records sharing the same key are guaranteed to land on the same partition via hash mod:

$$\text{partition} = \text{hash}(\text{key}) \pmod{\text{numPartitions}}$$

### Consumer Groups & Scalability
A Consumer Group represents a single logical subscriber. Each partition in a topic is consumed by exactly **one** consumer instance in the group at any given time. If you have 8 partitions, having more than 8 consumer instances in the group leaves the excess consumers idle.
keyIdea: Kafka treats disk as an append-only log, exploiting sequential I/O and OS page caches to outperform in-memory brokers at scale.

concepts.title: Zero-Copy Data Transfer
concepts.body: Kafka uses the `sendfile()` system call to transfer bytes directly from OS page cache to the network socket, bypassing user-space memory buffers.

concepts.title: In-Sync Replicas (ISR)
concepts.body: The set of broker replicas that are fully caught up with the partition leader's commit log.

examples: Uber streaming trillions of daily driver telemetry pings through Kafka clusters into Apache Flink.

resources.title: Kafka: The Definitive Guide (Narkhede et al.)

quiz.prompt: If a Kafka topic has 6 partitions and a consumer group has 10 worker instances, how many workers will actively consume data?
quiz.explanation: Each partition is assigned to at most one consumer in a group. Excess consumers beyond the partition count remain idle.
